overview: EROAD is a New Zealand-founded transport-technology company that sells in-vehicle telematics hardware bundled with a subscription SaaS platform for fleet management, regulatory compliance (New Zealand electronic Road User Charges, US Electronic Logging Device/IFTA tax reporting), safety and vehicle tracking. It operates through three regions -- New Zealand (its largest, most profitable and most defensible market as the incumbent electronic RUC provider), North America (a subscale, loss-making business being deliberately right-sized after a major customer loss and a NZ$134.7m FY26 goodwill/intangible impairment against the 2021/22 Coretex acquisition), and a smaller but fast-growing Australia. The company is dual-listed on the NZX and ASX (ticker ERD on both) and reports in NZD with a 31 March fiscal year end. FY26 was a year of upheaval -- a boardroom activist challenge, two CEO transitions, and a strategic reset -- and the company enters FY27 under an incoming, externally-hired CEO (David Leach, starting 12 October 2026) tasked with moving the business 'from reset to execution.'

business_model.summary: Revenue is a hardware-plus-subscription model: EROAD installs an in-cab telematics unit (largely rented/bundled rather than sold outright) and charges a recurring monthly SaaS subscription per contracted unit covering RUC/ELD compliance, fleet tracking, safety and fuel-tax reporting. FY26 subscription revenue was $185.9m of $195.2m total revenue (~95%), making the business predominantly recurring; the balance is transactional hardware and fee revenue. Management tracks Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR, $174.3m at FY26 year end) and monthly ARPU (Average Revenue Per Unit, $60.88 group-wide at FY26) as the core KPIs, alongside Asset Retention Rate (contracted-unit retention) by region. Historically EROAD also disclosed Future Contracted Income (FCI), a multi-year backlog metric reflecting the length of customer contracts. For FY27, management has explicitly declined to give top-line revenue guidance ('it just doesn't feel prudent to give top-line guidance... if we do give you guidance, we want to be able to guarantee that we can deliver it'), instead committing only to group free cash flow positivity -- a materially lower-visibility guidance regime than prior years.
business_model.customer_type: B2B -- commercial trucking/freight fleets, waste and utility operators, government/transport agencies; ranges from small-to-medium fleets to large enterprise accounts (EROAD defines 'Enterprise' as >$100k ARR); NZ also has an emerging B2G/B2C dimension as universal electronic RUC could extend the model to light vehicles
business_model.geographic_mix: New Zealand $102.0m (52% of FY26 revenue, +1.1% YoY), North America $74.4m (38%, -7.1% YoY), Australia $18.8m (10%, +40.3% YoY); unit count 124,470 NZ / 87,830 North America / 26,089 Australia at FY26 year end

competitive_position.market_position: Dominant, first-mover incumbent in New Zealand electronic RUC (management states ~86% of heavy-vehicle and ~85% of light-vehicle eRUC by value processed through EROAD, and 56% of NZ heavy-vehicle RUC kilometres on its platform); a much smaller disrupter/challenger brand in the fragmented but growing Australian market, now with a marquee enterprise reference customer (Cleanaway); a subscale, declining-share player in the vastly larger and more competitive North American ELD/fleet-telematics market, where Samsara, Geotab, Motive and Verizon Connect are far larger, better-funded and increasingly commoditising the hardware layer

moat_factors.description: First and largest electronic RUC provider in New Zealand since 2009, with deep integration into NZTA/government processes, brand recognition among fleet operators, and a nationwide installer network -- durable but not immune to reform (see risks)
Hardware fitted in-cab plus multi-year contracts and compliance workflows create switching friction once a fleet is onboarded; NZ asset retention rate was 91.9% at FY26

Two decades of accumulated fleet, safety and RUC/ELD compliance data and process knowledge across three regulatory regimes; management frames this as a structural barrier versus 'software-only' rivals given the complexity of hardware, integrations and compliance

Strong brand recognition in NZ; positioned as a credible 'disrupter' challenger brand in Australia, now backed by a large enterprise proof-point (5-year Cleanaway contract, 3,000+ heavy vehicles, on track for full deployment November 2026)

EROAD is subscale relative to Samsara, Geotab, Motive and Verizon Connect, who have far larger R&D budgets, broader platforms and more data; this contributed directly to the loss of its largest US customer (Old Dominion Freight Line, ~$9m ARR, 10,000+ units, non-renewal disclosed February 2026) to a cheaper competitor amid tariff-driven cost pressure

weaknesses: North America (38% of group revenue) is structurally subscale against much larger, better-capitalised US competitors and has been in revenue/ARR/unit-count decline (ARR -19.8% and units -15.9% in FY26), with asset retention the weakest of the three regions at 80.1%
Group profitability has been repeatedly disrupted by one-off costs, accounting-estimate changes and a large impairment, making underlying earnings power hard to assess from reported GAAP figures
Heavy reliance on a single very large customer loss (Old Dominion) materially moving group results shows customer concentration risk in North America

History of major capital-structure and governance stress: the 2021/22 debt- and equity-funded Coretex acquisition led to integration problems, a near-total write-off of the North American intangible/goodwill base, two CEO changes within 12 months, and an activist shareholder (Ampfield Management, ~17% stake) publicly contesting board composition in 2026

growth_drivers: New Zealand universal electronic RUC: the NZ Government has continued to progress its plan to replace fuel excise duty with distance-based electronic RUC for all ~4.7 million vehicles (including light passenger vehicles); Transport Minister Chris Bishop expects legislation to pass in 2026, with a public consultation on supporting regulations that closed 12 June 2026 and government market engagement on technology/delivery timelines through 2026, targeting implementation as early as 2027 -- EROAD frames this as a 'once-in-a-generation' expansion of its addressable market from the small share of vehicles currently on RUC to the full national fleet, though the eventual provider/collection model, and therefore EROAD's share of the opportunity, remains undecided

Australia enterprise expansion: ARR +73% YoY to A$21.9m in FY26, underpinned by the 5-year Cleanaway agreement (3,000+ heavy vehicles, A$5m+ ARR with fixed annual escalators, option to extend a further 3 years) tracking toward full implementation by November 2026, and a stated strategy to 'roll out the AU playbook' and expand enterprise sales presence in a market EROAD frames as fragmented and winnable

Disciplined North American repositioning toward free-cash-flow neutrality rather than growth, which should stem the region's cash drain even without a return to growth -- explicitly no longer competing head-on for growth against better-funded US telematics platforms

New, externally-hired CEO (David Leach, starting 12 October 2026) with a track record scaling SaaS ARR (grew Cin7's ARR more than five-fold to over $110m) brought in specifically to move the company 'from reset to execution,' following a year in which the board and executive team were substantially rebuilt

AI-driven operating leverage: management continues to invest in AI ('AI Native' strategic pillar) for internal workflow automation, platform modernisation and enhanced customer/data insights, aimed at improving margins without proportional headcount growth

Completion of the 4G hardware upgrade programme (73,000 units upgraded, ~88% renewal rate) removes a multi-year drag on reported free cash flow and should improve reported (not just normalised) FCF from FY27
Continued new-product cadence in the core telematics/asset-tracking range (e.g., ETrack G70 and Oyster3 asset trackers launched mid-2026) broadening the addressable use cases beyond powered vehicles

business.description: Competing against far larger, better-funded rivals (Samsara, Geotab, Motive, Verizon Connect) with greater R&D budgets and data scale; EROAD lost its largest US customer (Old Dominion, ~$9m ARR, ~10,000+ units, non-renewal effective February 2026) to a competitor offering a cheaper solution amid tariff-driven freight-volume pressure, directly triggering the FY26 impairment and strategic reset

A single customer non-renewal (Old Dominion) was large enough to materially move group ARR, revenue and drive a $134.7m impairment -- North America's enterprise-weighted customer base leaves the region exposed to similar step-changes

EROAD has had two CEO transitions within roughly 12 months: co-CEO David Kenneson resigned October 2025, successor Mark Heine then announced his own resignation (after almost 11 years at the company) effective June 2026, and a new externally-hired CEO, David Leach, does not start until 12 October 2026 -- an unusually long leadership vacuum/handover period for a company mid-turnaround, during which Executive Chair John Scott has run the business in an executive capacity; the new CEO inherits a transformation programme he did not design and must now demonstrate delivery ('from reset to execution')

US hedge fund Ampfield Management built a stake up to ~17% through 2026, nominated three directors and sought removal of two incumbents at a contested, rescheduled June 2026 AGM; the board's slate narrowly prevailed (director elections passed with margins as low as ~70.6%, turnout ~67.5% of shares), which commentators characterised as 'hardly a ringing endorsement' -- ongoing tension with a large, vocal shareholder is a distraction risk and could resurface at future meetings if turnaround progress disappoints
North America asset retention rate fell to 80.1% at FY26 (from higher historically), well below NZ's 91.9% and Australia's 95.8%, evidencing accelerating churn in the weakest region

financial.risk: Balance sheet impairment and net working capital deficit
financial.description: FY26 goodwill/intangible impairment of $134.7m cut net assets from $331.7m to $172.3m and drove a $161.1m net loss; as at 31 March 2026 current liabilities exceeded current assets (a net working capital deficit), though the FY26 accounts are prepared on a going-concern basis and management notes this is not expected to result in a cash outflow

Bank facilities ($65m limit, syndicate of ANZ, BNZ and Kiwibank) extended to October 2027 with covenants including net leverage reducing over time and a minimum interest coverage ratio; total liquidity was $49.0m against $16m of net debt at FY26 year end (H1 FY26 liquidity was higher at $62.3m against $7.7m net debt, reflecting the impairment/loss impact and seasonal working capital in H2) -- modest headroom for a company still absorbing transformation costs and a CEO transition

FY26 saw a $10.7m reclassification of R&D from capex to opex after introducing a minimum capitalisation threshold, plus a shortened useful economic life on intangibles (3-5 years from 5-10 years) -- both signal historically aggressive capitalisation that is now being unwound, and the pattern of frequent 'change in accounting estimate' items (accounting for $18.2m of FY26 EBIT impact) makes reported earnings volatile and comparability across periods difficult

Reports in NZD but North America (USD) and Australia (AUD) subsidiaries expose consolidated ARR/revenue to currency translation; FY26 ARR was reported as -0.5% in NZD but -1.4% in constant currency, showing FX partially flattered the headline number

regulatory.risk: NZ universal RUC collection model uncertainty
regulatory.description: The Government's move to universal electronic RUC is EROAD's single biggest opportunity but also a structural risk to its current incumbency: legislation is targeted for passage in 2026 (consultation on supporting regulations closed 12 June 2026) with implementation targeted as early as 2027, but the eventual Code of Practice, provider-approval process and market structure remain undecided; EROAD has publicly opposed NZTA acting as both regulator and retail eRUC provider and proposed a low-cost ($40) smart-tag device for mass-market uptake, indicating the collection model could be opened to new entrants or centralised in ways that erode rather than extend EROAD's current dominant position (currently ~86% of heavy-vehicle and ~85% of light-vehicle eRUC by value)

Management directly attributed the loss of its largest US customer to tariff policy compressing freight volumes (~10% reduction cited) and pushing customers toward cheaper telematics alternatives -- an ongoing macro/trade-policy risk to the North American customer base

regulatory.risk: Data privacy in a universal RUC rollout
regulatory.description: Extending distance-based road charging to millions of light/passenger vehicles raises privacy considerations that have already been flagged publicly by the NZ Privacy Commissioner, which could shape technical/consent requirements for any provider including EROAD

macro.description: North American revenue is directly linked to US trucking/freight volumes, which have been pressured by tariffs and a soft freight cycle; a prolonged downturn would continue to pressure the region EROAD is trying to stabilise

EROAD is a micro-cap (market capitalisation roughly NZ$180-200m as of late September 2026) with historically volatile, thinly-traded shares -- making entry/exit and price discovery difficult for investors, and amplifying the impact of concentrated shareholders such as Ampfield

Modest net borrowings ($16m at FY26 year end) mean direct interest-rate sensitivity is limited relative to larger leveraged infrastructure peers, but a still-recovering balance sheet increases refinancing sensitivity to any rate or credit-market deterioration

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global fleet telematics/SaaS compliance is a structurally growing category (electrification, safety mandates, ELD/RUC compliance, fuel-efficiency and emissions tracking), but the North American segment has become intensely competitive and increasingly commoditised at the hardware layer, compressing pricing power for subscale players; New Zealand's shift to universal electronic RUC is a rare, largely non-discretionary, policy-driven expansion of the addressable market for RUC-specialist providers, now progressing through 2026 legislative and regulatory consultation stages
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate -- revenue is subscription-based and relatively sticky, but new unit sales/installs and hardware revenue track freight and transport-sector activity, and North American revenue is exposed to US trucking-freight cyclicality and trade policy
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate -- modest absolute debt levels but still-thin liquidity headroom means funding costs and covenant compliance matter more than for a larger, better-capitalised peer
key_input_costs: In-vehicle hardware/semiconductor components (telematics units, now on 4G)

recent_developments.event: EROAD announced it will combine its previously-promised standalone operational/strategic update with its H1 FY27 half-year results and investor briefing, to be held together in November 2026 (results due ~19 November 2026 per market calendars); Executive Chair John Scott said a combined briefing bringing together financial performance, strategic progress, leadership transition and operational execution would give investors 'greater value' than a standalone update

EROAD announced the appointment of David Leach -- an experienced NZ technology-sector CEO (most recently CEO of Javln, previously CEO/executive director of Cin7 where he grew ARR more than five-fold to over $110m, plus prior roles at ezyVet, Qrious and Orion Health) -- as new Chief Executive Officer, effective 12 October 2026, completing the board and leadership overhaul that began in October 2025; Executive Chair John Scott called him 'the right leader for Eroad as we move from reset to execution'

EROAD launched two new asset-tracking hardware products (ETrack G70 and ETrack Oyster3) extending its device range to non-powered/powered asset tracking use cases; total shares on issue increased to ~189.05m following a Long Term Incentive Plan share issuance

Contested Annual Shareholders' Meeting (rescheduled from the normal AGM date) at which activist US hedge fund Ampfield Management (built a stake to ~17.1%) sought to remove directors John Scott and Sara Gifford and install three of its own nominees; shareholders rejected the removal proposals and the board's own nominees (including Ampfield-nominated Ian Whiting) were elected, but margins were narrow (as low as ~70.6% support on some resolutions, ~67.5% of shares voted), reflecting what commentators called 'hardly a ringing endorsement' of the board amid ongoing turnaround uncertainty; director Barry Einsig did not seek re-election

FY2026 annual results (year ended 31-Mar-2026): revenue $195.2m (+0.4%), ARR $174.3m (-0.5%), reported EBIT loss of $(155.9)m (Normalised EBIT $2.9m) driven by a $134.7m non-cash impairment of North American goodwill/intangibles plus $18.2m of accounting-estimate changes and $5.9m of one-off costs; net loss after tax $(161.1)m; normalised FCF $14.4m (FCF margin 7.4%, down from 12.1% in FY25); management declined to give specific FY27 revenue/ARR guidance, instead committing only to group free cash flow positivity, citing a preference not to give guidance it cannot guarantee to deliver

Old Dominion Freight Line, EROAD's largest North American customer (~$9m annual revenue, 10,000+ driver-monitoring units, acquired via the 2021/22 Coretex acquisition), did not renew its contract and switched to a lower-cost competitor; CEO Mark Heine attributed the loss in part to US tariffs reducing freight volumes (~10%) and pushing customers toward cheaper telematics alternatives

H1 FY2026 interim results (six months to 30-Sep-2025): revenue $99.1m (+3.3%), positive free cash flow of $6.2m, liquidity $62.3m against $7.7m net debt, but a reported net loss of $144.2m driven by the same $134.7m North American goodwill/intangible impairment applied in October 2025; FY26 guidance reset to reflect the ANZ pivot and the pending NA customer non-renewal: revenue $197-203m, ARR $175-183m, FCF margin 5-8% (which the FY26 actuals subsequently came in modestly below on revenue/ARR)

Strategic reset: the Board applied the North American goodwill/intangible impairment, appointed John Scott as Executive Chair to lead a business-wide reset, and co-CEO David Kenneson (who had led the North American push) resigned; company shifted from a global to a regional operating model and explicitly refocused strategy on New Zealand and Australia, with North America to be run for cash generation rather than growth; Mark Heine (previously co-CEO) subsequently announced in early 2026 his own resignation as sole CEO, effective June 2026, after almost 11 years at the company

guidance.as_of: FY2026 Annual Results (25 May 2026); reaffirmed via 17-September-2026 announcement of a combined H1 FY27 results/strategic update in November 2026

guidance.management_commentary: Executive Chair John Scott described FY26 as reflecting 'the past' with the business intending to 'look different' going forward, citing an 'erosion of focus on our customers' as the core cause of the year's problems and outlining five strategic priorities (Operational Excellence, Product Excellence, Customer Intimacy, becoming AI Native, and 'Winning Universal eRUC'). On appointing new CEO David Leach (effective 12 October 2026), Scott said the past year had been spent 'strengthening the board, reshaping leadership, and refocusing on customers,' and that Leach is 'the right leader for Eroad as we move from reset to execution.' Leach said his focus will be 'improving customer outcomes, strengthening execution and ensuring we invest our time and capital in the areas that produce the highest returns.' The company will provide a comprehensive combined update on H1 FY27 financial performance, transformation progress, leadership transition and operational execution in November 2026, its first substantive market update under the new CEO.

bull_case: New Zealand universal electronic RUC is a rare, policy-driven expansion of EROAD's core addressable market, with legislation targeted for passage in 2026 and implementation as early as 2027, leveraging an incumbency position (~85-86% of eRUC value processed) that a new entrant would need years to replicate

The FY26 impairment and reset draw a clear line under the failed North American growth strategy -- ANZ (NZ + Australia) alone generated $19.5m of normalised free cash flow in FY26, and management's strategy of making North America merely cash-flow neutral rather than continuing to fund its losses should materially improve consolidated free cash flow if executed

A completed leadership and governance overhaul -- new Executive Chair, new CFO, new regional GMs, a contested-but-resolved board election, and now an externally-hired CEO (David Leach, starting October 2026) with a strong SaaS-scaling track record -- removes much of the transition uncertainty and puts a credible, unconflicted operator in charge of execution rather than the executives who presided over the North American misstep

Australia is EROAD's fastest-growing and highest-momentum segment (ARR +73% YoY), underpinned by a large, multi-year enterprise contract (Cleanaway) approaching full deployment (targeted November 2026), in a market EROAD frames as fragmented and winnable using its NZ playbook

The share price has recovered somewhat off its 2026 lows (around NZ$1.00-1.15 as of late September 2026, versus an August low near NZ$0.985) but remains a small fraction of the company's 2021 capital-raise price (NZ$5.58/share) and well below Volaris/Constellation Software's 2023 all-cash takeover offer of NZ$1.30/share -- a sign the market may still be pricing in a pessimistic turnaround outcome, leaving asymmetric upside if the ANZ-focused reset succeeds under new leadership
bear_case: The turnaround remains unproven and has now run through two CEOs in 12 months (David Kenneson resigned October 2025, Mark Heine's own resignation followed within months, effective June 2026) with a roughly four-month gap before new CEO David Leach starts (12 October 2026) -- an unusually long handover for a company mid-transformation, and Leach inherits a strategy and impairment history he did not create

North America (still ~38% of group revenue) remains structurally subscale against Samsara, Geotab, Motive and Verizon Connect, evidenced by the weakest asset retention rate of the three regions (80.1% at FY26) and a large customer loss driven partly by cheaper competitor offerings -- there is no guarantee 'cash-flow neutral' is achievable before further customer attrition erodes the base further

Management has withdrawn formal top-line (revenue/ARR) guidance for FY27, committing only to group free cash flow positivity -- a meaningfully lower disclosure and visibility standard than prior years, which increases the risk of unpleasant surprises and makes it harder for investors to hold management accountable to specific targets

An activist shareholder (Ampfield Management, built to ~17% of the register) contested board composition at a rescheduled June 2026 AGM; while the board's slate prevailed, margins were narrow (~67.5% turnout, some resolutions passing with as little as ~70.6% support), signalling fragile shareholder confidence that could resurface as a distraction or renewed contest if the new CEO's early results disappoint

The NZ universal eRUC opportunity cuts both ways: the exact collection/provider model remains undecided even as legislation nears passage, and EROAD's own public opposition to NZTA acting as retail provider signals real uncertainty about whether the eventual regulatory design preserves or erodes its current incumbency advantage; balance sheet capacity also remains thin ($49.0m total liquidity and $16m net debt at FY26 year end, against covenants stepping down through the October 2027 facility maturity), leaving limited room for further setbacks without additional capital or covenant stress
